Eight demos established a variant where a uniform-background sparse-marker field is transformed by coloring only the background cells strictly between consecutive markers on each row or column. Demos 5 and 8 directly show both horizontal and vertical intervals; e.g. demo5 row9 markers at c2 and c25 color c3–24, and demo8 c0 markers at r0 and r4 color r1–3. Snapshot marker locations from the input and process consecutive pairs only. Task ID d795d9b6 has other variants (including rays), so verify current demos.

A fresh task-d795d9b6 instance had sparse marker grids and three highly varied demos, showing the task ID alone does not identify the operation. Earlier incorrect first submission extended intervals across all marker endpoints/lines, coloring unsupported regions; correct approach is consecutive marker pairs only. For implementation: snapshot input; for each row, sort marker columns and fill open intervals between neighbors; then each column, sort marker rows and fill open intervals. Preserve endpoints and unrelated cells. This instance's test had 21x8; accepted output is derivable by that algorithm.

The second demo had larger bg=5/marker=0 grid and demonstrated substantial changed areas, apparently the same row/column intervals between neighboring markers. Analyze by *consecutive* marker pairs rather than treating every marker line or all spaces as fill. Some cells may appear as changed beyond a visually simple interpolation at first glance; map exact coordinates if another recurrence tests a similar version.

A previous skill note claimed eight demos were available; current actual instance proved a similar interpolation mechanism but at three demos, with a strongly atypical third demonstration of two adjacent markers. Do not require minimum marker counts; a pair is enough. D795d9b6 family can feature multiple variants, including rays or other patterns, and historical ID-linked notes are only hypotheses. Ground each new instance in its current demos and any selector evidence; request more if the task’s behavior is not explained by every observed pair.
